issue_title: Coating presets 'Dual-layer AR' and 'V-coating' reflect more than bare glass
issue_body:
**Where:** `src/coating_designer.py:172-191`, `:315-329`

The dual-layer preset stacks quarter-wave Ta2O5 under quarter-wave MgF2. Two quarter-wave layers only cancel when the inner index is about `n2 * sqrt(ns)` ~ 1.70; 2.10 makes the coating worse than none. The V-coating thicknesses look arbitrary (x1.2 and x0.9 factors). These values feed `Lens` reflectance and ghost analysis.

**Repro (BK7, 550 nm):**

| Preset | Reflectance |
|---|---|
| Uncoated | 4.216% |
| MgF2 single-layer | 1.284% |
| Dual-layer AR | **4.345%** |
| V-coating | **18.949%** |

**Fix:** use Al2O3 (n~1.63) under MgF2 for the quarter-wave pair, or a real V-coat with solved non-quarter thicknesses. Add a test that every AR preset is below the uncoated reflectance at the design wavelength. (The transfer-matrix maths itself checks out.)
pr_title: fix(coating): an AR preset must not reflect more than bare glass
pr_body:
## Description

fix(coating): an AR preset must not reflect more than bare glass

Both anti-reflection presets were physically wrong. **The transfer-matrix code
was not the problem — the inputs were.**

### Dual-layer AR

It used Ta2O5 at n=2.10 under MgF2. Two quarter-wave layers cancel only when the
inner index is `n_outer · √n_substrate` — about **1.70** for MgF2 on BK7. At 2.10
the pair *amplified* reflection.

### V-coating

Its broadband design was expressed with unexplained `×1.2` and `×0.9` factors.
That is an assertion, not a design, and it stacked Ta2O5 again.

### What they do now

| BK7 at 550 nm | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| uncoated | 4.216 % | 4.216 % |
| MgF2 single layer | 1.284 % | 1.284 % |
| **dual-layer AR** | **4.345 %** | **0.0014 %** |
| **V-coating** | **18.949 %** | **0.266 %** |

The dual-layer now **scores every ordered pair of catalogued materials with the
module's own transfer-matrix routine** and keeps the best. The bare substrate is
a candidate — so the preset cannot come out worse than doing nothing, which is
exactly the property the old hard-coded pair violated.

The V-coating's outer thicknesses are **solved numerically**, minimising mean
reflection across 400–700 nm and starting from the bare substrate's cost, so the
search can only improve on it. It now beats bare glass at **every wavelength in
the band**, not just at 550 nm where it used to be 4.5× worse.

## Two things stated rather than glossed

**The solved V-coat gives SiO2 about 7 nm.** That is a real outcome of minimising
band-average reflectance — the middle layer contributes little once the outer pair
does the work — but it is thin. A fabrication minimum would be worth applying if
these presets are ever used for a real coating specification.

**One test I wrote asserted two substrates get different dual-layer materials.**
That is not a property the design has: the search is a coarse grid over seven
indices, so neighbouring substrates can legitimately share the best pair while both
remaining correct. It now asserts the **index condition**, which is what actually
decides the cancellation.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #457

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after —
      the issue's exact table reproduces (`4.345%` dual-layer, `18.949%` V-coat)
- [x] Verified by reverting **each preset separately**:
  - the dual-layer back to hard-coded Ta2O5/MgF2 → **12 of 14 fail**
  - the V-coating back to asserted `×1.2`/`×0.9` thicknesses → **8 of 14 fail**
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_coating_presets tests.test_coating` — 37 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1887 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 233 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8 src/coating_designer.py` — **4 findings, identical to `master`**
- [x] Coverage includes:
  - **the user's check**: every AR preset reflects less than uncoated
  - the dual-layer's index condition (`n_inner = n_outer·√n_substrate`) within 10%
  - the inner layer being the higher index and both layers genuinely quarter-wave
  - the inner layer *not* being Ta2O5 at 2.10 — named explicitly, since that is the bug
  - the V-coat helping at 450/550/650 nm individually, not just at the design point
  - the V-coat earning its extra layers against the single-layer preset
  - six substrates from n=1.40 to n=2.00, each improving on bare
  - the inner index tracking the substrate across that range

### Why the acceptance criterion is "better than bare" and not a magic number

The obvious test — assert reflectance equals 0.0014% — would pin the *search*,
not the *physics*, and would break the next time the catalog gains a material. The
property a user can check at a glance is that a coating labelled "anti-reflection"
reflects less than no coating at all. That holds for every preset, on every
substrate tested, by construction rather than by luck.
